# Per-IP burst limit of 20 clicks a minute

> Each IP is limited to 20 clicks per minute; clicks exceeding this are marked invalid but still recorded in Kafka.

_Part of [Ad click tokens and fraud checks](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md)_

When an ad click arrives, we check whether the IP address has already clicked too many times in the current minute. To avoid storing raw IPs in Redis, each IP is hashed with SHA-256 using the secret key as a salt. We maintain a Redis counter for each hashed IP per minute—the counter increments with each click and automatically expires to keep Redis clean. If the count exceeds 20, we mark the click as invalid (`valid: 0`) so it won't be charged to the advertiser, but we still record it to Kafka for auditing. This stops rapid-fire fraud from a single IP without unfairly blocking legitimate users who happen to click multiple times.

**Look at:** [`click` in ads.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/ads.service.ts#L9)

## Pieces

- [Per-minute time buckets with 120-second auto-expiry](per-minute-bucketing-and-expiry.md): Clicks are grouped by minute as `Math.floor(Date.now() / 60_000)`; each minute bucket is counted separately in Redis and expires after 120 seconds.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| cache | ``adclick:ip:{`ipHash`}:{minute}`` | Redis counter incremented with each click from an IP in a given minute. Compared against `IP_BURST_PER_MIN` (20) to set the `valid` flag on the click record. |

## Watch out

- The counter expires in 120 seconds, not 60—this 60-second buffer after each minute boundary prevents race conditions as time buckets roll over.
- Invalid clicks are still published to Kafka with `valid: 0`; they're not dropped, just marked non-billable for auditing and fraud analysis.
- The IP hash is salted with the deployment's secret key, so the same IP hashes differently across environments.
